content:
Local weather is one of the most underrated variables in Apple Home automation setups. Over the past few years, I've used various sensors to take care of everything from reminding me to let faucets drip during freezing weather, to adjusting sprinkler schedules through Eve Aqua on hot days. Eve Weather has been part of my setup for a while, and since it gained Matter support a few years ago, it has become extremely useful in my home.

HomeKit Weekly is a column series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

If you've been following HomeKit Weekly for a while, you'll know I really love those automation setups that run on their own. Smart home accessories are only truly useful when they can perform tasks automatically. This is exactly why I've always recommended building your smart home around a single ecosystem rather than mixing and matching. Even in the Matter era, I don't want to use a bunch of different platforms at the same time. For me, that platform is Apple Home. I tend to use Eve devices because they have always prioritized privacy, and as long as you stick with Matter-supported local control, you can skip the cloud account requirement. Eve has also been actively supporting Matter and Thread in recent years. This is exactly the kind of development you'd want to see.

Eve Weather provides three pieces of data from a small device: temperature, humidity, and barometric pressure. It has an IPX4 water resistance rating, and its aluminum casing means it doesn't look out of place outdoors. My unit is installed outside. The highly localized readings it provides often differ by a few degrees from the data shown in the Apple Weather app. Honestly, this difference matters most during extremely hot or cold weather. When the temperature drops to 31°F and freezes your pipes, but the app shows 34°F, you'll definitely wish you had consulted local data.

One of Eve Weather's underrated features is its built-in 12-hour weather trend display. It uses barometric pressure changes to predict weather patterns. You can tell at a glance from the visual icons whether the weather is trending toward clear skies, clouds, rain, or storms. This small detail provides great value, letting you quickly get the picture without opening your phone's app.

Here are a few automation scenarios you can build using Eve Weather:

  • When the temperature drops below freezing, turn on a colored light to remind family members to let the faucets drip.
  • When outdoor humidity is particularly high, turn on the dehumidifier.
  • If it's already raining and the forecast shows more rain coming, delay the sprinkler system from running.
  • Ask Siri directly for the current front yard temperature without having to step outside.

Matter and Thread support in 2026

Several years ago, Eve released a free firmware update that added Matter support to Eve Weather. If you already own this device, you can upgrade through the Eve app. The Matter version supports Apple Home as well as Amazon Alexa, Google Home, and SmartThings. The sensor itself is exactly the same—it's just become cross-platform, making the device future-proof so you won't have to worry even if you decide to switch your primary smart home ecosystem later.

Eve Weather is what's known as a "Minimal Thread Device." This means it communicates via Thread but doesn't route data traffic. The routing work is handled by always-on "Full Thread Devices," such as Eve Energy or Eve Water Guard. The more Full Thread Devices you have, the more robust and stable your Thread network becomes, and battery-powered devices like Eve Weather benefit directly from this stability.

You also don't need to create an Eve account. Unless you choose to, all operations stay local. The Eve iPhone app is an excellent tool for visualizing and tracking historical temperature, barometric pressure, and humidity trends. It's a very interesting way to help you spot patterns and make smarter decisions about things like lawn watering or energy management.

I have several HomePod minis placed around the house and rely on my Eero 6E network to support Thread. Eero added Thread support through software, providing a solid foundation for accessories like Eve Weather, keeping the devices connected and running quickly.

Eve Weather Wrap-up

The only thing I'd still like to see improved is the addition of a rechargeable battery design. The battery life currently lasts several months, but I'd prefer a USB-C port like the one on the Eve Room. That said, Eve Weather remains one of my favorite Apple Home accessories. It's minimalist, looks great, and thanks to Matter, works well across all major platforms. If you want to bring local weather information into your smart home and trigger useful automation scenarios, Eve Weather is an easy recommendation for me.

You can buy it from Amazon or directly from the Eve Store.
